target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram webhook shutdown could leave owned resources active when an early teardown step failed: a synchronous `server.close()` throw, a `bot.stop()` rejection, or a transport-close rejection could skip later cleanup (bot stop, undici transport close, webhook status, diagnostic heartbeat). Ingress-worker `stop()` could also race on repeated calls and leave `worker.terminate()` rejections unobserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Independently guard each ordered webhook shutdown phase via `runTelegramWebhookShutdownPhases` so one sync/async failure cannot skip later owned cleanup, and wrap the path so fire-and-forget abort listeners never leak unhandled rejections. Startup failure cleanup uses `.catch(() => undefined)` so cleanup noise cannot mask the original startup error. Ingress-worker `stop()` shares one in-flight promise and observes terminate rejections.

Non-goals: no UI drive-by edits; no committed `proof-*.mts` (local-only configured-token proof + vitest cases).

Collision check: searched open PRs for webhook shutdown skip / ingress terminate rejection; no stronger same-fix open competitor.

## User Impact

Operators restarting or aborting a Telegram webhook account no longer risk leaked transports, stale webhook connected status, or leftover diagnostic heartbeats when one shutdown step fails. Process logs no longer see unhandled rejections from webhook/ingress shutdown paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `aac474a46e7803ea688ba9f398c70240b86a7555`
- Rebased onto current `origin/main`.
- Surface: 6 `extensions/telegram/` files only.

Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook-shutdown.proof.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts -- --run -t "does not leak unhandled|does not skip"
```

```
 ✓ negative/positive/valid shutdown phase cases
 ✓ ingress-worker stop idempotent + terminate rejection observed
 ✓ webhook unhandled/skip regressions — passed
```

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Configured Telegram bot token + production `startTelegramWebhook`: local webhook listener starts, `setWebhook` registration failure / abort still runs owned shutdown without unhandled rejections.

### Environment

- OS: Linux x86_64
- Node: v24.18.0
- head: aac474a46e7803ea688ba9f398c70240b86a7555
- Bot: real BotFather token via local `tokenFile` (redacted; `getMe` ok / username present)

### Exact commands run

```bash
PROOF_HEAD=aac474a46e7803ea688ba9f398c70240b86a7555 TELEGRAM_TOKEN_FILE=$HOME/.openclaw/credentials/telegram-bot.token \
  node --import tsx proof-telegram-configured-webhook-lifecycle.mts   # local only; not committed
```

### Observed output after fix

```
node=v24.18.0
head=aac474a46e7803ea688ba9f398c70240b86a7555
bot_token_present=true

[case 1] configured bot: local listen then setWebhook URL rejection runs shutdown
  log: webhook local listener on http://127.0.0.1:41365/telegram-webhook
  error: telegram setWebhook failed: Call to 'setWebhook' failed! (400: Bad Request: bad webhook: An HTTPS URL must be provided for webhook)
  ok: start threw (expected registration failure)
  ok: local listener started
  ok: no unhandledRejection
  info: throwMsg=Call to 'setWebhook' failed! (400: Bad Request: bad webhook: An HTTPS URL must be provided for webhook)
  info: elapsed_ms=3196

[case 2] configured bot: abort during startup cleans without unhandledRejection
  error: telegram getMe failed: Aborted delay
  ok: abort produced no unhandledRejection
  ok: abort path completed
  info: outcome=rejected:Aborted delay

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 5 passed, 0 failed
```

### Evidence

- Real bot token accepted (`bot_token_present=true`; prior `getMe` ok).
- Case 1: local listener bound, Telegram API `setWebhook` rejected (HTTPS required for public URL in this harness), start threw, **0 unhandledRejection** — owned shutdown path ran after registration failure.
- Case 2: abort during startup completed with **0 unhandledRejection**.
- Vitest covers negative nested-control-flow skip vs guarded continue + ingress-worker terminate observation.

### What was not tested

- Public HTTPS ingress + successful `setWebhook` advertise to Telegram (this harness used loopback HTTP publicUrl to force registration failure after listen). No live chat message round-trip.

## Risk / Compatibility

Medium-low (`merge-risk: availability` for teardown sequencing). Fail-soft: phase failures are logged; later owned cleanup still runs. No config/SDK surface changes in the PR diff.
